```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
```

## What it does

misscox rebuilds the simulation study of Marshall, Altman, Royston and Holder (2010). It simulates
prognostic cohorts like the German Breast Cancer Study Group 2 data, deletes values of four
covariates under MCAR, MAR, MNAR or a combined mechanism, handles the missing data by complete case
analysis, single imputation or one of seven multiple imputation methods, and fits the full Cox
model with Rubin's rules.

Marshall A, Altman DG, Royston P, Holder RL. Comparison of techniques for handling missing covariate
data within prognostic modelling studies: a simulation study. *BMC Medical Research Methodology*
10:7 (2010). doi:10.1186/1471-2288-10-7

## Install

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("jeonglab-bcm/fossil/PMC2824146/package")
```

```{r load}
library(misscox)
packageVersion("misscox")
```

## Example input

The missingness design of the paper: the share of the incomplete cases that miss each covariate,
and each pair.

```{r shares}
shares <- read.csv(example_path("missing_shares.csv"))
shares
```

And one simulated cohort of 1000 cases with 25% of cases made incomplete under MAR.

```{r cohort}
x <- read.csv(example_path("example_cohort_mar25.csv"))
dim(x)
head(x)
colSums(is.na(x))
mean(!complete.cases(x))
```

## Run the method

The odds ratios between the missingness indicators (Table 3) follow from the design: the shares
become whole cases of 1000, rounded half up.

```{r table3}
t3 <- table3_odds_ratios()
t3
```

Handle the missing data of the example cohort with three of the methods and fit the Cox model.
Five imputations here to keep the tutorial quick; the paper used twenty.

```{r methods}
fits <- lapply(c("CC", "SI", "MICE_PMM_notrans"), function(m) handle_missing(x, m, m = 5, seed = 1))
res <- do.call(rbind, fits)
data.frame(method = c("CC", "SI", "MICE_PMM_notrans"), n = res$n_analysed,
           X2 = signif(res$est_X2, 3), se_X2 = signif(res$se_X2, 3),
           X3 = signif(res$est_X3, 3), se_X3 = signif(res$se_X3, 3))
```

## Compare with the expected output

Table 3 as printed in the paper, at printed precision (half a unit in the last digit):

```{r compare-t3}
exp <- read.csv(example_path("table3_expected.csv"), colClasses = "character")
printed_ok <- function(observed, printed) {
  d <- nchar(sub("^[^.]*\\.?", "", printed))
  abs(observed - as.numeric(printed)) <= 0.5 * 10^(-d) + 1e-12
}
ok <- sapply(c("pct5", "pct10", "pct25", "pct50", "pct75"), function(k) printed_ok(t3[[k]], exp[[k]]))
cat(sum(ok), "of", length(ok), "odds ratios match Table 3\n")
stopifnot(all(ok))
```

The full Cox model on the breast cancer data (`TH.data::GBSG2`) against the paper's linear
predictor:

```{r compare-lp}
lp <- read.csv(example_path("lp_expected.csv"), colClasses = "character")
b <- coef(fit_full_cox(gbsg_covariates()))
ok <- printed_ok(unname(b), lp$printed)
data.frame(term = lp$term, paper = lp$printed, ours = signif(unname(b), 4), match = ok)
cat(sum(ok), "of", length(ok), "coefficients match the paper\n")
stopifnot(all(ok))
```

## Your own data

`handle_missing()` takes a data frame with columns `X1` to `X7` (numeric; X5 to X7 coded 0/1),
`X8g` (tumour size group 1, 2 or 3), `time` (days) and `status` (1 = event), with `NA` where a value
of X2, X3, X5 or X8g is missing. The method is one of `method_labels()`: `CC`, `SI`, `NORM`, `MIX`,
`MIX_notrunc`, `MICE`, `MICE_PMM`, `MICE_PMM_notrans`, `AREG`. The result has, for each
coefficient, the pooled estimate (`est_`), its standard error (`se_`), the Wald p-value (`p_`) and
the 95% interval (`lo_`, `hi_`), then the likelihood ratio p-value, Nagelkerke's R2, the D
statistic, the predicted 2-year survival at the mean covariates and the number of cases analysed.

To run the study itself: `generation_parameters(gbsg_covariates())` builds the generator,
`run_replicate()` runs one replicate over mechanisms, levels and methods, and
`summarise_replicates()` gives bias, coverage and the other figure quantities.

## The full reproduction

The pipeline that reruns the paper's study with this package, and compares every table, figure
point and claim with the paper: <https://github.com/jeonglab-bcm/fossil/tree/main/PMC2824146>.
